## Setup

```{r}
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
```

## Read in data and create an analytical data set

### First: Read countries.txt

```{r}
#| echo: true

countries <- read.table(
  "../data/raw/countries.txt",
  header = TRUE
)

dim(countries)
```

There are `r nrow(countries)` countries and `r ncol(countries)` columns in this data set.

### Second: Read regions.txt

```{r}
#| echo: true

regions <- read.table(
  "../data/raw/regions.txt",
  header = TRUE
)

dim(regions)
```

There are `r nrow(regions)` countries and `r ncol(regions)` columns in this data set.

### Third: Create an analytical data set

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Check variable names
names(countries)
names(regions)

# Identify the ISO country code column
possible_names <- c(
  "country_code", "iso3", "iso3c",
  "iso_code", "code", "ISO3", "ISO"
)

code_col <- intersect(possible_names, names(countries))[1]

# Standardize ISO codes
countries <- countries |>
  mutate(
    country_code = toupper(
      trimws(as.character(.data[[code_col]]))
    )
  )

regions <- regions |>
  mutate(
    country_code = toupper(
      trimws(as.character(country_code))
    )
  )

# Keep only countries included in the study
study_regions <- regions |>
  semi_join(countries, by = "country_code")

dim(study_regions)
```

The analytical data set contains `r nrow(study_regions)` countries.

## Tabulate countries by region and sub-region

### Number of countries by region

```{r}
#| echo: true

region_counts <- study_regions |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(
    Count = n_distinct(country_code),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Count))

kable(
  region_counts,
  col.names = c("Region", "Count"),
  caption = "Number of Countries by Region"
)
```

### Number of countries by sub-region

```{r}
#| echo: true

sub_region_counts <- study_regions |>
  group_by(sub_region) |>
  summarise(
    Count = n_distinct(country_code),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Count))

kable(
  sub_region_counts,
  col.names = c("Sub-region", "Count"),
  caption = "Number of Countries by Sub-region"
)
```

## Data visualization using ggplot

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7

ggplot(
  study_regions,
  aes(
    x = fct_infreq(sub_region),
    fill = region
  )
) +
  geom_bar() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Countries by Sub-region",
    x = "Sub-region",
    y = "Number of Countries",
    fill = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
